correctness.rationale: The canonical simplex-orbit fixed-set triangulation identifies the two-layer horizontal-edge orbit with each graph edge, and each fixed rung with a pendant leaf, giving exactly M(W(G)). Every invariant matching extends to a perfect prism matching by filling unused rungs. The recursive augmented-poset matching toggles the private edge at the least residual vertex in its zero block and recurses on blocks where a core edge is selected; every cross-block unmatched Hasse arrow points into the zero block. Induction proves acyclicity and identifies the unmatched faces precisely with the p(G) perfect matchings, all of dimension |V|/2-1. Dropping the augmented empty-face pair leaves one critical vertex. A CW complex with just a zero-cell and p same-dimensional cells has the asserted integral sphere-wedge homotopy type, including k=1 and no-perfect-matching cases. The standalone checker independently enumerates and verifies all 76 graphs with n<=4 and six larger examples; these tests do not replace the all-graph induction.

originality.rationale: The closest full primary source, Agarwal and Basak arXiv:2608.30601 (19-page v2 inspected), classifies nonequivariant matching-related complexes of specific circular and Mobius ladder graphs. The known special case of the layer-exchange fixed locus for G=C_n is explicitly excluded as new. No inspected theorem or indexed published-record comparison entails the global arbitrary-base-graph fixed-locus classification, the PL orbit model including the equality of two different fixed loci, or the p(G)-indexed integral homotopy formula. A general earlier whiskered-graph theorem could remain unindexed.
residual_risks: A general matching-complex theorem for fully whiskered graphs might predate the indexed sources under another terminology; search failure alone cannot establish absolute novelty.
The previously known circular-ladder fixed-locus theorem covers G=C_n; only the strict global arbitrary-G extension and its uniform proof are asserted as new.
Some peripheral primary sources were inspected at abstract level, not in complete full text; no all-document noncoverage assertion is made for those.

value.rationale: The result turns a natural equivariant topological invariant of arbitrary graph prisms into the classical perfect-matching enumeration p(G), not merely a special-parameter recomputation. It proves one uniform integral homotopy classification for all finite graphs, including disconnected and dense graphs, via an explicit global discrete-Morse matching; p(K_{2k})=(2k-1)!! and p(K_{k,k})=k! produce large natural families. The fixed-point homotopy has no torsion even if the full matching complex is substantially more complicated. This precision can support further equivariant and enumerative investigations without claiming a polynomial-time matching counter or complete equivariant homotopy type.
